summary: The note surveys creative financing options for start-ups and SMEs, beginning with a brief history from personal savings and angel investors to venture capital and crowdfunding. It illustrates each method with a dated case example, including partnerships, crowdfunding, microloans, equity crowdfunding, venture debt, corporate venture capital, government grants and incubators. It closes by pointing to emerging options like tokenization, cryptocurrency funding and revenue-based financing.
one_line: Overview of creative SME and start-up financing methods, from crowdfunding to venture debt and grants, illustrated with dated success stories from 2023-2024.
key_facts: Start-up financing in the mid-20th century relied mainly on personal savings, bank loans, and angel investors.
Venture capital firms became key players in the start-up ecosystem by the late 1970s and 1980s as a high risk-high reward option.

On September 10, 2023, Jessica Hynes secured a deal for her tech start-up CodeCraft Inc. through partnerships with established software development companies, whose backing included financial support.
On January 5, 2024, eco-friendly apparel start-up GreenThread launched a crowdfunding campaign on the platform SeedSpark; founders were Anna Larson and Michael Tunji.
By March 2024, GreenThread had raised 150% of its intended target, with pre-orders from around the world.

On October 8, 2023, Portland brewery owner Oliver Bates described how a microfinancing institution specializing in food and beverage gave him capital with a repayment plan tailored to cash flow, after banks refused a significant loan.
On February 15, 2024, 3D printing company InnoPrint used the equity crowdfunding platform ShareStarter; by April 2024 it had attracted enough investors to match its VC funding goals.
On December 12, 2023, med-tech start-up HealthInnovate used venture debt to scale operations while avoiding significant equity dilution.
On September 20, 2023, agritech start-up AgroCore received corporate venture capital funding from agricultural giant FarmFutures.
On November 1, 2023, SolarSolutions, a solar energy SME, was awarded a government grant for green technology initiatives, used for research and development.
EspritTech, an AI solutions start-up for SMEs, joined an incubator program on January 22, 2024 and emerged four months later with seed funding, partnerships and a refined business model.
Tokenization, cryptocurrency funding, and revenue-based financing are named as options gaining traction in the post-pandemic world.
